wealth.name: Glyph Wealth
wealth.title: Glyph Wealth | Net worth, spending and holdings in files you own
wealth.description: Glyph Wealth keeps accounts, spending, holdings and net worth as plain lines in your vault. Say a balance or bring in a statement. No bank login, and it never invents a number. Free for Mac and iPhone.
wealth.lead: Accounts, spending, holdings and net worth.
wealth.note: Every figure shown is made up for the pictures. Arithmetic on the numbers you give it, not financial advice. Apple silicon, macOS 26 or later.

imgs.alt: Today on the Mac: net worth counted, what is liquid and owed, an estimate left out of the figure, eighteen months of history and how long the money lasts
Accounts on the Mac, grouped as cash, investments, retirement, property and cards, each with when it was last read
Cash flow on the Mac: what a month costs, how much was kept, each month in, out and kept, and where the month went
Portfolio on the Mac: what is invested, the fees a year, and each holding's share
Scenarios on the Mac: months of runway if work stopped, the number to reach and the year it is reached under a poor, a normal and a good run
Glyph Wealth on iPhone: today's net worth with history and runway
Accounts on iPhone, grouped, each with its balance and when it was read
Cash flow on iPhone: a month's cost and each month in, out and kept
Portfolio on iPhone: invested, fees a year and each holding's share

features: It never invents a number
Every figure traces to a line you said or a file you brought in. What is not known says so, and is never shown as a zero.
Three kinds of certainty
Read from a statement, sourced from a note, or claimed. Totals add only the first two; an estimate is shown beside them, outside the figure.
Say it
Say a balance, a spend or a transfer in plain words. It reads the amount, the account and the date, and keeps your words beside what it understood.
Bring in a statement
CSV, OFX and QFX files. It shows the rows it read, the ones it already had and the ones it skipped, and says so when a file cannot be read.
No bank login
Nothing here holds a password to your bank. Numbers arrive by voice, by a file, or by confirming what a note in your vault already says.
Cash flow
What a month costs, how much of it does not stop, what was kept, and the charges that come back.
Portfolio
What is invested, the fees it costs each year and over ten, and when more than a fifth sits in one holding.
Scenarios
How many months the money lasts if work stopped, the number you are aiming at, and the year it is reached on a poor, a normal and a good run.
Papers and dates
The documents a tax year usually needs, ticked off as they arrive, and the dates that do not move.
Plain lines in your vault
Whole cents, one line per fact, append only. Each device writes its own file, so a synced folder never conflicts.
Tags
The same tags as the rest of the Glyph family, read from one register in your vault.
Mac and iPhone
The same screens on both, saved to the same vault.

omega.name: Glyph Omega
omega.tagline: From your mission to today's move
omega.title: Glyph Omega | Your mission, your goals and the next move, in files you own
omega.description: Glyph Omega keeps your mission, vision, values and goals as plain files in your vault, and breaks each goal down until what is left is the thing to do next. Talk through your day and review once a week. Free for Mac and iPhone.
omega.lead: Your mission and goals, broken down.
lines: Until what is left is the next move.
omega.note: The goals shown are made up for the pictures. Apple silicon, macOS 26 or later.

imgs.alt: Goals on the Mac, grouped by area of life, each with its next action, due date and progress
Today on the Mac: the north star in large type, the direction, and one next move
Mission on the Mac: vision, values in order, ambitions and objectives
One goal open beside the list: status, progress, due date, why it matters and its next actions
The weekly review: one goal at a time, its progress, how it is going and its next action
Glyph Omega on iPhone: the north star and what you said
Mission on iPhone: the north star, the mission and the vision
Goals on iPhone by area of life, and ambitions
Tags on iPhone, the same tags as the rest of the family

features: One north star
Your purpose in a sentence, at the top of Today and above everything else.
Mission, vision and values
Written once, in your words, with the values in the order you would keep them.
Goals by area of life
Health, money, learning and the rest, each goal with a due date, a measure and its progress.
Broken down to the next move
A goal is not finished being written until it has a next action. One that has none says so.
Talk through your day
Say where things stand. It proposes what changed on which goal and you confirm before anything is saved.
A review once a week
One goal at a time: move the progress, say how it is going, make sure there is a next action.
Your words are kept
What you said is saved first, word for word, before anything reads it.
Plain files in your vault
The same files your agents read. Nothing is stored anywhere else.
When the vault is away
It shows the last copy it read, says when that was, and writes nothing until the vault is back.
Tags
The same tags as the rest of the Glyph family, read from one register in your vault.
Mac and iPhone
The same goals on both, through your own hub.

crm.name: Glyph CRM
crm.tagline: The people and things you own
crm.title: Glyph CRM | Everyone and everything you deal with, as notes in files you own
crm.description: Glyph CRM keeps the people, places, organisations and things in your life as plain notes in your vault, linked to each other and filed by area of life, so every other Glyph app knows who you mean. Free for Mac and iPhone.
crm.lead: Everyone and everything you deal with.
lines: Kept as notes every Glyph app can read.
crm.note: Every person, company and note shown is made up for the pictures. Apple silicon, macOS 26 or later.

imgs.alt: A person's page on the Mac: attributes, links to where they work and live, and dated notes
An area of life on the Mac: what was logged, its tasks, its state and its files
An organisation's page on the Mac, with the people linked to it
Search on the Mac across people, places, organisations, things and notes
People on iPhone, each with the line that says who they are
Organisations on iPhone, each with who works there
Tags on iPhone: the one register every Glyph app reads
An area of life on iPhone: log a note or a task, and what is open

features: People, places, orgs and things
One page each, with the attributes you care about and nothing you do not.
Linked to each other
Works at, lives in, friend of, attended. A link is made once and shows on both pages.
Notes with a date
Say or type what happened. It lands on the right page, dated, in your words.
By area of life
Health, money, home and the rest, each with what was logged, its tasks and its files.
Yours, and everyone else
A page you saved is yours. The rest of the register is one tap away and never in the way.
The home of tags
Tags are kept here, in one register, and every other Glyph app reads the same ones.
Every Glyph app knows who you mean
Wealth, Well, Life and the others read these pages, so a name said anywhere is the same person.
Suggestions, not surprises
New people and facts heard in what you say are offered for a yes, never added on their own.
Plain notes in your vault
One file per page, readable anywhere, the same files your agents read.
Mac and iPhone
The Mac reads the vault directly; the iPhone reaches it through your own hub.

connect.name: Glyph Connect
connect.tagline: What your agents can actually reach
connect.title: Glyph Connect | Every app and tool your agents can reach, and what each may do
connect.description: Glyph Connect shows every app and tool your agents can reach, which ones need you, and what each may read and write. Cut one tool or switch a whole app off. Free for Mac and iPhone.
connect.lead: Every app and tool your agents can reach.
lines: And what each one may read and write.
Cut one tool, or a whole app.
connect.note: The connections shown are made up for the pictures. Apple silicon, macOS 26 or later.

imgs.alt: Reach on the Mac: how many apps your agents can reach, which need you, and what is open
Connections on the Mac: every app, filtered by state, kind and area of life
One app's page on the Mac: a switch for the whole app, and each tool's sync and chat switches
Every tool across every app on the Mac, with what each may do
Glyph Connect on iPhone: what your agents can reach
Connections on iPhone, with filters across state, kind and area of life
Chat on iPhone: ask what can be reached, or cut something off
Tags on iPhone, the same tags as the rest of the family

features: One number first
How many of your apps your agents can reach right now, and which ones need you.
Needs you
A sign-in that lapsed or a key that is missing is named, with the step that fixes it.
Every connection
Open, off, failing or not connected, filtered by kind and by area of life.
What each tool may do
Reads and writes are listed apart. A write changes something outside your vault and says so.
Cut one tool
Switch a single tool off in chat or in sync and leave the rest of the app working.
Or the whole app
One switch says whether agents may reach an app at all. It is instant and it is reversible.
No write runs unattended by accident
One click clears every write tool from sync, and one puts them back.
Ask it
Ask what can be reached, or say what to cut off, and it does it with an Undo.
Your registry, not a new one
It reads the app registry already in your vault and changes only the keys it owns.
Mac and iPhone
The Mac reads the vault; the iPhone reads it through your own hub.

well.name: Glyph Well
well.title: Glyph Well | Say how you slept, ate and felt, and see what tends to come before your worse days
well.description: Glyph Well is a health log you talk to. Say how you slept, ate and felt, and it shows what often came before your worse days, holds your lab results and gets a visit summary ready. It shows patterns and does not diagnose. Free for Mac and iPhone.
well.lead: Say how you slept, ate and felt.
lines: See what often came before a bad day.
Kept as plain files in your vault.
well.note: The log shown is made up for the pictures. Glyph Well shows patterns in what you log; it does not diagnose and is not medical advice. Apple silicon, macOS 26 or later.

imgs.alt: Today on the Mac: last night's sleep, heart rate and steps, a box to say how you feel, and one tap for a bowel movement
Insights on the Mac: the worst symptom of each day over sixty days, and what often came before the worse days
Food on the Mac: the foods you suspect, and how often symptoms followed each one
Labs on the Mac: each marker drawn against its range over time
A visit summary on the Mac: days logged, symptoms, bowel movements and medicines for the last thirty days
Glyph Well on iPhone: one day in the log, each entry under its tag
Insights on iPhone: symptoms over sixty days and what often came before them
Food on iPhone: your suspects and what followed them
Tags on iPhone, the same tags as the rest of the family

features: Say it
Talk or type a sentence and it becomes entries: the meal, the symptom, the sleep, each on the day it happened.
Saved as you say it
Nothing waits behind a Save button. Undo takes back what one sentence became.
What often came before
Counts of your own days: how often a symptom followed a food, a short night or a hard workout. Never a cause.
Bowel movements in one tap
The seven Bristol types as plain shapes, with colour, urgency and the rest when you want them.
Lab results against their range
Each marker over time, by marker or by the place that ran it.
A summary for the visit
Days logged, symptoms, medicines and results for the period, as one page or a PDF.
Questions for the appointment
Say them as they occur to you and tick them off in the room.
Your wearable beside your words
Sleep, heart rate, steps and workouts from Garmin and Apple Health, next to what you said.
Research from your own files
Ask about your own entries and results. It does not search the internet and gives no advice.
Plain files, your vault
Every entry is a line in a file you own. fru.dev does not collect it and cannot read it.

life.name: Glyph Life
life.title: Glyph Life | What is due, what charges, what lapses, and the jobs that keep it in order
life.description: Glyph Life shows what is due this week, the subscriptions about to charge, the cover about to lapse, your filed documents and the recurring jobs that watch them. Read from your vault. Free for Mac and iPhone.
life.lead: What is due, what charges, what lapses.
lines: Keep it or cancel it, before it charges.
life.note: The bills, policies and documents shown are made up for the pictures. Apple silicon, macOS 26 or later.

imgs.alt: Due on the Mac: three subscriptions charging this week with Keep it and Cancel it, and one policy lapsing
Documents on the Mac: two waiting for a yes, and the filed ones with their expiry dates
Money out on the Mac: what leaves each month and each year, one line per subscription
Workflows on the Mac: a renewal watch opened to its steps, with what it watches for and when it is done
Glyph Life on iPhone: three charges this week, each with Keep it and Cancel it
The lists on iPhone: documents, money out, cover and workflows
Chat on iPhone: ask what is due this week, or say what to cancel
Workflows on iPhone: one due now, one active, one staged

features: What is due, first
The charges and lapses of the coming days, counted in one line at the top.
Keep it or cancel it
Each charge asks for a decision before its date, and remembers the one you gave.
Money out
What your subscriptions cost a month and a year, and the ones with no price yet said as such.
Documents
What has been filed, by kind, with the date each one expires.
Waiting for you
A document the filer could not place asks for a yes, and each yes teaches it a rule.
Cover
Your policies and the day each one ends, so none lapses unnoticed.
Workflows
The recurring jobs, what each watches for, and when it last ran.
Ask it
Ask what is due this week, or say what to cancel.
No new store
It reads what is already in your vault and writes only your decisions.
Mac and iPhone
The Mac reads the vault; the iPhone reads it through your own hub.
